catalog.summary: Standalone 'Cosmic Duality Chain 1-4' reproducer with the P3, SalPhaseIon-small (SA), Phase3.2-inner (P32B) and Cosmic Duality (CD) blobs embedded; asserts sha256 of each 'decrypt' and includes a 'MatrixSumlist\nAnsToo' SA false-path audit; all outputs are binary

Brute force over letter(a-i)->bit-string permutation maps of dbbi+faed; 4/5/6/7/8-bit regrouping, EBCDIC/charset decodes, keyword search; private-key->address step is a broken placeholder (address = '1'+pubkey hex)
Earlier version of the same Chain 1-4 reproducer (same blobs, passwords, mask, lengths); shows how the 1168-byte 'mystery' slice and chain4 pass E_C+E_S+E_B[:2] are built
Generic Persian-language null-cipher / Bacon / vowel-consonant / word-length decoding toolbox reading keys.txt; no GSMG constants
Tries a short Matrix-themed password list (+case variants) on the embedded Cosmic Duality blob; its own EVP routine derives only a 16-byte key (wrong for AES-256)
catalog.author: HushHush

catalog.summary: Decodes the 4 SalPhaseIon streams (a/b binary + a-i/o digit ciphers) into known tokens, then tries openssl ciphers/KDFs with token combos and sha256s on a MIS-TRANSCRIBED copy of the SA blob
catalog.author: HushHush

catalog.summary: Generic Bacon-type / null-cipher / vowel-binary toolbox (Persian/English text, keys.txt); no GSMG constants
Beaufort (key THEMATRIXHASYOU) with an unknown byte->letter mapping recovered by English-tetragram hill-climb on an external blob.bin; generic corpus, no embedded result
Reproduces the 39 'extra door' P2PKH addresses of puzzlehunt issue #110 from slices of the disputed 1327-byte cosmic plaintext; itself labels the route UNVERIFIED and the addresses empty
catalog.author: issue #110 poster (GitHub handle in file, not recorded)

catalog.summary: Persian-alphabet letter-class (3 groups) -> binary/base3 experiments and null-word tests; no GSMG constants
Generic OpenSSL-compatible AES helper (EVP_BytesToKey-SHA256 or PBKDF2-SHA256 10000) with printable-ratio filter; no constants

leads.claim: 'Chain1': SalPhaseIon small blob decrypts (AES-256-CBC, EVP_BytesToKey MD5) with the concatenated tokens to a 79-byte BINARY plaintext split K_C1(32)|K_C2(32)|E_C(15).
leads.method: openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -md md5, pass = token concatenation
leads.self_verifying: No. 80-byte ciphertext -> 79 bytes means pad byte 0x01, which a wrong password gives about 1 time in 256. The output is binary, not text. The script itself shows a second padding-valid SA password ('MatrixSumlist\nAnsToo'), so padding-valid SA passwords are not unique.

leads.claim: 'Chain2': Phase 3.2 inner blob (P32B) decrypts with password = uncompressed WIF of K_C1 (chain1[:32]), MD5 KDF, giving 79 binary bytes K_S1|K_S2|E_S. This is the only step with some cross-blob support, if only that one WIF was tried.
leads.self_verifying: Weak. Again only 0x01 padding (p~1/256 per attempt) and binary output. The evidence is worth something only if few WIF/slice variants were tried, and that number is unknown. A check with our own oracle would confirm or refute the padding claim but would not prove correctness.

leads.claim: 'Chain3 / cosmic_correct': Cosmic Duality blob decrypts with raw 32-byte pass = XOR of sha256(token) over 7 tokens (the matrixsumlist pair cancels), MD5 KDF, giving 1327 binary bytes.
leads.method: XOR of SHA256(tokens) as binary passphrase, EVP_BytesToKey MD5, AES-256-CBC
leads.self_verifying: No. Pad byte is 0x01 again (1328 -> 1327) and the output is binary. The maintainer (Naddiseo, quoted in from_issue110_addresses) calls it a 1/256 PKCS#7 false positive. Because of XOR cancellation, many token sets give the same pass. This is the community 'cosmic' decrypt behind issue #110.

leads.claim: 'Chain4': chain3[158:1326] XORed with an 8-byte repeating mask starts with 'Salted__' and decrypts (MD5 KDF) with pass E_C|E_S|E_B[:2] to 1151 binary bytes (marker 2b2d, header28, operand 37); the trailing byte 0x3a ':' is called a mystery tail.
leads.method: 8-byte XOR unmask then openssl aes-256-cbc md5
leads.self_verifying: No. The 'Salted__' match proves nothing because any 8 bytes can be XORed into 'Salted__' by picking the mask. The pass is an ad hoc slice concatenation, the pad is 0x01 again, and the output is binary. All 4 chain steps having pad=0x01 is the expected pattern for false positives; real plaintexts would have pad 1..16.

leads.claim: Phase 2 page blob (P3) decrypts with the ASCII hex of sha256('causality'), EVP_BytesToKey SHA256, giving 648 bytes.
leads.self_verifying: Yes (readable Phase 3 text), but this stage is already solved.

leads.claim: Alternate SA preimage 'MatrixSumlist\nAnsToo' gives valid PKCS#7 padding on the SA blob, but its WIF does not open P32B. The author calls it a false path.
leads.self_verifying: No (binary). Useful only as evidence that padding-valid SA passwords are easy to find, which undercuts Chain1.

leads.claim: 39 'extra door' P2PKH addresses = Base58Check(0x00 || CC[X*32+16:X*32+32] || BE32(X)), X = 0..38, over the disputed 1327-byte cosmic plaintext. The file says all are empty on-chain, not funded gates, UNVERIFIED.
exact_strings: CERTIFIED_PLAIN_SHA=4f7a1e4ef6c5581e32505c019657cb7b030e90232d33f011aca6a5e9c081 (60 hex; drops 'fe4b' vs the stage2753 value)
cosmic_A.bin is made up by llms
leads.method: raw byte slicing, no curve operation
leads.self_verifying: No. Addresses built from raw slices with no private key cannot prove anything, and the prize address is not among them.

leads.claim: The SalPhaseIon a/b streams and a-i(+o=0) digit ciphers decode to the four known tokens. The embedded SA ciphertext is mis-transcribed, so every decrypt attempt in this script is invalid.
leads.method: a=0/b=1 binary to ASCII; letters to digits to hex to ASCII
leads.self_verifying: Yes for the token decodes, which are already known. Any negative result from this script is meaningless because of the corrupted blob.

leads.claim: Matrix-themed passwords (enter, matrixsumlist, lastwordsbeforearchichoice, thispassword, neo, trinity, morpheus, zion, followthewhiterabbit, thereisnospoon, wakanda, shuri, ...) and simple variants tried on the CD blob. No success is claimed, and the KDF bug (16-byte key) would hide a real hit anyway.
leads.method: MD5 EVP with AES-128 key length (buggy)
leads.self_verifying: Yes, if run with a correct oracle (readable text). These are trivial and already covered by phrase-password sweeps.

leads.claim: All letter->bit-string permutation maps of dbbi/faed, regrouped into 4/5/6/7/8-bit chunks and searched for keywords (salvation, zion, trinity, bank, looking, bitcoin, btc), plus a hex->privkey->balance check whose address derivation is a placeholder and never matches real addresses.
leads.self_verifying: Not applicable; it is a blind search with no reported result.

leads.claim: Beaufort with key THEMATRIXHASYOU after hill-climbing an unknown byte->letter substitution on a raw blob (first 500 bytes, scored by English tetragrams from a generic corpus).
leads.self_verifying: No. Hill-climbing a free 256->26 mapping overfits and will produce English-like text from random bytes. The blob is unspecified, and the THEMATRIXHASYOU Beaufort is already known from the Phase 3.2 stage.
